statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20% (watch) because the NQ session high of 30,961.50 has stopped extending and price has retraced about 27 points away from it, while Stress of 57% (elevated) reflects a 10-year yield at 5.175% in its sixth consecutive weekly climb against roughly 70% odds of an October Fed increase.
recommendation: Tail sits at the WATCH floor and remains below the block threshold. The concentrated whipsaw window is 12:15-15:15 UTC, covering August durable goods orders at 12:30 UTC, the US cash open at 13:30 UTC, the final September Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations release at 14:00 UTC and the delayed second-leg hour that can follow. US cash markets close at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures close for the week at 21:00 UTC, reopening at 22:00 UTC on Sunday; forecast hours inside that halt carry reduced Confidence because no live price path exists to observe.
headline: The NQ session high stalls at 30,961.50 and price retraces about 27 points off it, easing Tail to the WATCH floor while a 15.38 VIX, a flat 2-year and falling oil leave the amplifier stack unaligned
body:
NQ December futures trade at 30,934.75, up 168.00 points or 0.55%, with the session recorded between 30,679.00 and 30,961.50 from a 30,726.50 open. The decisive change from the previous hour is a loss of upward extension: the session high is unchanged at 30,961.50 rather than advancing again, and price has retraced roughly 27 points away from it instead of holding about 7 points below it.

That reverses the two amplifiers that lifted Tail to 22% an hour ago. A high that stops extending and a retracement away from the extreme are the observed opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks, so Tail eases to the WATCH floor at 20%. It does not fall further, because the pullback is shallow at about 10% of the observed range, price remains in the upper part of a band that is only 0.92% wide, and two US releases fall within the next three and a half hours.

Cross-asset evidence does not support a one-way path. VIX is 15.38, down 1.85%, inside an unusually tight 15.29-15.64 range. The 10-year yield is 5.175%, up 1.2 basis points, in a 5.153-5.189% range and short of the 5.225% intraday peak reached earlier in the week, which was its highest since July 2007; the 2-year is flat at 4.895% and the 30-year sits at 5.465% after a post-2004 high. A firm long end that is no longer extending intraday is a Stress input rather than a Tail amplifier. WTI is 92.93, down about 1.78%, and Brent 105.38, down about 1.15%, after reports that negotiators are exploring a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz alongside a lifting of the US blockade of Iran. Falling oil removes an amplifier, though Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep the energy track two-sided. European cash is firm, with STOXX 600 +0.6% at 640.43 by 08:21 UTC and on course for a near-1% weekly gain that would snap a three-week losing streak.

Shared Finviz context was collected at 08:12 UTC and is both stale against the 90-minute freshness threshold and partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. It is therefore not used as evidence for current structure, and every cross-asset value above comes from an independent primary source fetched this hour. Its available latest-session sections are explicitly not real-time and are noted only as prior-session tone: semiconductors were 7 of 7 positive with a mean of +1.59%, while megacaps were split 4 to 4 with a mean of +0.235%, a pattern more consistent with rotation than with index-level one-way structure.

Stress is 57%. The Nasdaq-100 is advancing against a long end that has climbed for six consecutive weeks, with roughly 70% odds on CME FedWatch attached to an October increase after New York Fed President Williams described a further hike this year as reasonable, and with the final September Michigan inflation-expectations reading due at 14:00 UTC where the one-year consensus is 4.6% against 4.0% prior. That is a genuinely difficult environment in which high Stress coexists with Tail below the blocking threshold. Confidence is 87%: the NQ level and session extremes come from a live primary quote timed at 10:15 UTC, VIX, the 2-year and 10-year yields and oil from primary sources, and today's release times and consensus figures are cross-verified across two independent calendars. The unavailable Finviz futures section and the absence of a live cash-index print before the open are the only material gaps.
lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 published Claude assessments held Tail between 17% and 24%, with Stress in a 54-59% elevated band and Confidence between 85% and 88% throughout. The 24 September European morning traded trend-down near the top of the WATCH band before decaying through the US session, and from 17:00 UTC the sequence settled into the low Tail band with a normal mode overnight. Tail then lifted to the WATCH floor at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC on a trend-up mode as NQ cleared its earlier overnight high, eased to 19% at 08:00 UTC when that high stopped extending, and returned to 22% at 09:00 UTC when the high advanced again. This hour the extension has stopped and a retracement has occurred.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-way drift inside and slightly below a 0.92%-wide overnight band through the European morning, with Tail at the WATCH floor now that the session high has stopped extending. Risk concentrates between 12:15 and 15:15 UTC, where August durable goods orders, the US cash open and the final Michigan sentiment and inflation-expectations reading fall in sequence into a market pricing roughly 70% odds of an October rate increase. The mode is expected to turn event/whipsaw there, with Tail peaking at 26% and crossing into the block band for two hours around the 14:00 UTC release and its potential delayed second leg. That peak reflects a credible yields-led mechanism rather than observed structure, and Tail decays quickly if retracements occur and the 10-year holds its 5.153-5.189% range. The afternoon carries no verified scheduled release, leaving a power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close on the final session of the week. CME equity index futures then close for the week at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen before 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so the final thirteen forecast hours fall inside a halt: Tail drops to the low band because a halted market cannot produce a pathological path, Stress decays more slowly against carried weekend gap exposure, and Confidence steps down into the medium-low band because no live NQ price path exists to observe.
